records.text: Jeffrey Epstein did not work for Israel or Mossad and did not run a blackmail ring for them.
records.speaker: Naftali Bennett

appearances.snippet: Said, quote, as a former Israeli Prime Minister, with the Mossad having reported directly to me, I say to you with 100% certainty, the accusation that Jeffrey Epstein somehow worked for Israel or the Mossad running a blackmail ring is categorically and totally false.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The DOJ/FBI review reported no incriminating client list and no credible evidence of blackmail of prominent individuals. Former Israeli prime minister Naftali Bennett publicly denied that Epstein worked for Mossad. Those sources support parts of the statement, but Bennett's denial is not independent proof that Epstein had no relationship with Israeli intelligence, so the compound categorical claim is not fully established.

records.text: Mossad has not been active in the United States since the Jonathan Pollard scandal of 1987.
records.speaker: Naftali Bennett

appearances.snippet: I followed up with the former Prime Minister, Naftali Bennett, and what he told me is that Mossad has not been active in the United States since the war against the United States, since the Jonathan Pollard scandal of 1987,

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Reporting says Israel formally pledged after the Pollard affair not to conduct espionage in the United States and that the ban was widely regarded as having held in the narrow Mossad sense. Other U.S. intelligence assessments have nonetheless described continuing Israeli collection against U.S. targets. The absolute claim that Mossad has been wholly inactive in the United States since Pollard is therefore too broad.
